newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLO yield to head for 5.80% in 1,2 months - dealers.
newsitem.headline: OLO yield to head for 5.80% in 1,2 months - dealers.

text.p: The yield on the benchmark Belgian government bond (OLO) dipped below six percent on Wednesday, marking the start of a rally which could take it to 5.80 percent in the next one to two months, dealers said.

Prices rose on the back of gains in the German and U.S. markets, but volumes remained on the thin side. "We saw some buyers. There is now some solid ground for the beginning of a larger movement," a trader said.
The 10-year benchmark BE286= yielded 5.99 percent at 101.86 at 1440 GMT, off a high at 102.05 set about half an hour earlier. The yield eased from 6.02 percent late on Tuesday.

The trader said markets had been helped by technical gains by the June Bund future, which he now saw rising to 101.20 or 101.60. It was up 0.21 at 100.43 at 1445 GMT. The OLO future gained 0.23 at 120.00.
He said the five to 10-year section of the OLO yield curve flattened in the course of Wednesday, while the 10-20 year end steepened slightly.

Dealers said bears who had been pointing to a likely cycle of U.S. interest rate rises had been pushed aside by bulls flagging positive trends in Europe -- low price and wage inflation, and no near-term upturn in leading interest rates.
"It is all a question of how far you want to look ahead," a trader said.
Fresh clues as to the course of U.S. rate policy will come on Friday afternoon in the shape of retail sales and factory

Growth of U.S. retail sales is seen easing off, while PPIs are expected to show slower growth year-on-year. If in line with the forecasts, both sets of numbers would be bond-positive, but that does not imply markets will rally, dealers said.
"The U.S. market has had a distinct bear tone to it," one said. "It is marked by fears for a rate hike."

Dealers said optimism on the European markets early in the week that economic and monetary union (EMU) would go ahead as planned and the tough Maastricht Treaty criteria would be applied strictly resurfaced.

One analyst said that in the next three months lower U.S. Treasuries and a pick-up in the German economy might push the yield on the benchmark 10-year Bund up to 6.50 percent from about 5.90 percent on Wednesday.
This would impact OLOs. With Germany being Belgium's largest trading partner, Belgian rates are tied closely to German ones.

Looking ahead, the analyst said, the back-up in German rates would be limited in view of the currently low inflation, modest wage increases with the upside scope limited by a lax labour market, and a likely slowdown in U.S. growth.
German rates and yields, and consequently Belgian rates and yields, would not rise much beyond 6.50 percent, she added.
Other analysts said that cash which recently had been going into the short end in the wake of the U.S. Fed's recent rate rise might now be shifting into the longer end.
Some targetted yield levels at around 5.90 percent on the 10-year OLO by the end of the second quarter.

The afternoon optimism spread to the shorter end with rates on three-month Treasury bills easing to 3.25/27 percent from 3.28/29 on Tuesday and the one-week repo rate at 3.17/21 percent, down from 3.18/22.
